llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Tamaton MCP setup guide, but its default setup grants broad mail, storage, calendar, billing, and paid-spend authority and includes an unsafe credential-in-URL install command.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Tamaton and an MCP bearer token are expected for this service, but the token can access private mail, calendar, storage, billing state, and paid operations if created with the documented default scopes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill requires curl and external calls to tamaton.com, which fits the MCP integration, but the documented install snippet sends the bearer credential as a URL query parameter even though the same artifact warns that secrets should not be placed in URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions advise requesting only needed scopes, but the copy-paste setup example requests broad privileges by default, including billing:write and mail:send, without separating optional capabilities into narrower opt-in credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No bundled executable code, background worker, local persistence hook, or privilege escalation mechanism was found; persistence is limited to the user's configured environment variable or MCP configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Email, documents, storage, calendar, search, credits, subscription, and x402 payment behavior are disclosed and mostly purpose-aligned, but the default registration example combines sensitive data access, outbound email, billing write access, and a 100000-credit spend cap in one credential.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use the narrowest scopes needed, avoid billing:write unless you deliberately want billing changes, set a much smaller or zero spend cap where possible, and do not use the install?key=... URL workflow; pass the token only through an Authorization header or a local MCP secret reference.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Billing and paid add-ons are disclosed in the manifest description and body text, so the capability is not hidden; however, the default scope set still materially over-grants billing authority for basic setup.
[E1] expected: External transmission to tamaton.com is expected for registering and using a hosted MCP productivity service; this signal is not evidence of unrelated exfiltration by itself.
[T09] unexpected: Authentication to the service is expected, but placing the full bearer credential in the install URL query string is an avoidable credential-handling risk and conflicts with the artifact's own warning.
[T05] unexpected: The broad default registration example is not least-privilege for a first connection because it combines sensitive read access, email sending, billing write permission, and paid-spend authority in one token.
